## Natural history notes

A small prominent moth characterized by mottled gray-brown to tan forewings with darker patches and wavy markings that help it blend into bark or dead leaves. In Florida, it appears to be a localized or rare species, with records tied to the state and the Punta Gorda name reflecting its Florida association. It is likely found in wooded or shrubby habitats where suitable host plants and sheltered resting sites occur; adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on plant foliage and serve as prey for birds, spiders, wasps, and other insect-eating animals.
